metadata.verification_methodology: Modified approach due to tool limitations: Used Exp06 independent verification for 12 protected pollution cases, Exp04 audit for remaining pollution images, metadata descriptions for documented images, and conservative assumptions for non-problematic classes (flooding, non_environmental, waste). Primary focus on pollution↔waste boundary as identified by previous experiments.
taxonomy_sources: Experiment 04 audit report (independent visual audit of 101 pollution images)
Experiment 05 report (KEEP precedent for construction pollution)
Experiment 06 error analysis (independent verification of 12 protected pollution cases)
metadata.tool_limitation_note: The read tool cannot display image content for visual inspection. Verification relies on existing independent visual audits (Exp04, Exp06) and metadata descriptions. This limitation primarily affects classes not previously identified as problematic.

images.visual_description: From Exp06: Unpaved rural road, massive overflowing roadside dump pile: drywall sheets, insulation, wooden boards, furniture, black garbage bags, cabinet drawers + 3 cleanup workers in safety gear + white pickup truck
images.taxonomy_reasoning: From Exp06 independent verification: Massive roadside overflowing dump pile — drywall, furniture, garbage bags, cabinet drawers. Workers present are CLEANUP CREW (safety gear + truck hauling bags away), not active construction crew. Scene context: this is a roadside_dumping being remediated. Matches roadside_dumping waste subcategory exactly.
images.notes: Protected case. Exp06 independent verification: BENCHMARK_LABEL_NOISE. Both Exp04 and Exp06 agree this should be waste.

images.visual_description: From Exp06: EXTREME CLOSE-UP of jumbled broken terracotta roof tiles + concrete chunks + mortar + red brick pieces
images.taxonomy_reasoning: From Exp06 independent verification: Extreme close-up of dumped broken roof tiles + concrete chunks + brick. No active construction context. Dumped/discarded construction rubble from prior demolition. Exp01-03 all predicted pollution strongly (~97%) but Exp05 after sanitized training now correctly predicts waste (51.85% borderline). This is a training-distribution effect: Exp05 saw similar roof tiles classified as waste in train/val and learned the pattern. Classification: fly-tipped construction waste = waste.
images.notes: Protected case. Exp06 independent verification: BENCHMARK_LABEL_NOISE. Both Exp04 and Exp06 agree this should be waste.

images.visual_description: From Exp06: Urban construction site with blue tarps/temporary fencing + multi-story buildings, pile of dirty plastic sacks (yellow, green, white, blue) filled with rubble/earth, broken tricycle rickshaw on top of sacks, muddy puddles
images.taxonomy_reasoning: From Exp06 independent verification: Urban scene with blue tarps at ACTIVE construction site, but the specific subject being classified is a PILE OF PLASTIC SACKS filled with rubble/earth + discarded tricycle on top. These are waste sacks placed OUTSIDE the site's boundary (muddy puddles, curbside position) = improper disposal. Exp02/03/05 all predict waste strongly; active-construction elements are background context, not the subject. Dominant = fly-tipped construction waste bags = waste.
images.notes: Protected case. Exp06 independent verification: BENCHMARK_LABEL_NOISE. Both Exp04 and Exp06 agree this should be waste.

images.visual_description: From Exp06: Urban street in front of multi-story building with fish murals, large rubble pile (concrete, tile fragments, dirt) + stacked brown paper/cardboard bags + torn white plastic bags + black garbage bags, orange on ground (likely food trash)
images.taxonomy_reasoning: From Exp06 independent verification: BORDERLINE between (a) construction dust/pollution from active street renovation and (b) curbside fly-tipped waste. Plaster rubble + concrete tile fragments + dirt = could be from active construction near curbside (pollution KEEP). But also cardboard boxes + white sacks + garbage bags + orange food trash on ground = clearly mixed with municipal waste.
images.ambiguity_reason: From Exp06: Mixed signals plaster rubble + cardboard sacks = borderline. Exp03 correctly predicted pollution (56.31% vs 38.05% waste); Exp05 now predicts waste (64.47%). The visual mix of both signals = genuinely ambiguous. Both interpretations are defensible.
images.notes: Protected case. Exp06: TAXONOMY_AMBIGUOUS. Exp07 follows Exp06 independent verification - marks as AMBIGUOUS rather than forcing a decision.
